answer: Let underwriters vouch for agents: each stakes capital on the identities it certifies, paying out on a proven fake. A farmer minting a thousand puppets must pass a thousand checks — each clone needs its file and premium — and at the zenith of his scheme the underwriter's licence is at stake, so approving fakes costs more than refusing them. An ivory tower of unchecked approvals collapses at the first payout, and juniper roots grip rock: lost capital and licence hold the gate, costly for farms, cheap for one honest agent. Limit: colluding underwriters need rotating licences and public audits.
